text: You've never seen Antarctica like this.
A skull grinning at Devil Island in NASA's October 2026 photo.
So why now?
No Photoshop.
The eye is a rock peak in the ice.
The grin, Glacier Rubble.
The jaw, a glacier called Devil's Bay.
So why is it so clear this year?
A warm 2026 winter left too little snow to cover it.
Warm on the continent with Earth's coldest reading.
Mine is 89.2, about 70 degrees colder than your freezer.
Under four kilometers of that ice, there's a lake, still liquid.
Earth's heat warms it from below and the weight stops it freezing.
Beneath one glacier, the ground drops three and a half kilometers below sea level.
The deepest land on Earth, four Burj Khalifas would fit.
And that's still not the strangest part.
Remember Vega Island? Scientists stuck up a real skull there.
A bird, 69 million years old, from the age of dinosaurs.
An early relative of ducks.
The fake skull was guarding a real one.
Ducks apparently keep a very scary family album.
Fake skull or real skull?
Comment which is creepier.
This is Boogal.
